mike_pm: Hey folks — I pushed a first-pass PRD for Dedicated capacity (SLA / sizing / autoscale). Please review: https://redwood.docs/prd/dedicated-capacity-v1
anya_eng: Skimmed — major gaps: acceptance criteria for autoscale and steady-state throughput. Adding quick checklist.
anya_eng: ```
Acceptance criteria:
- 99p latency < 200ms for gen requests under committed throughput
- Sustained provisioned throughput: 2.5k tokens/sec per reserved pool (configurable)
- Autoscale: scale-up within 60s when sustained GPU util > 80% for 30s
- Scale-down: cooldown 3m, avoid flapping; prefer additive steps (+1 GPU) up to 10% incremental
- Cold-start: warm-pool resume < 500ms, cold provisioning < 3s for burst-only paths
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to smaller model variant within 150ms if 99p latency breached
- Rollout safety: canary -> ramp -> full, automatic rollback on repeatable SLA breaches
```
sam_sre: Need explicit error-budget policy + detection. Suggest: if error-budget burn rate > 2x for 10m, trigger failover and paging. Also add metrics: tail_latency_99, fallback_rate, token_throughput, queue_depth.
lina_prod: From customer conversations: priority is predictable tail latency and contractual uptime. We should include a cost-vs-guarantee table (commit size vs unit cost) and a downgrade policy (how we communicate and bill during degradation).
raj_infra: Operational constraints: scaling granularity should avoid noisy-neighbor spikes. Suggest cap: max scale rate 2 GPUs / min per pool, with global budget throttle to prevent cross-tenant starvation. Also we need admission control for large bursts.
mike_pm: Good points. Proposal for canary: 1% traffic for 30m -> 10% for 60m -> 100% over 4h. Auto-rollback if 99p latency regresses > 20% vs baseline for two consecutive 5m windows. Anyone object?
anya_eng: Fine, but tech note: fallback latency budget must include model swap + cache rebuild. Add requirement: KV cache warming within 90s. Also add unit/integration tests for routing policy.
sam_sre: Runbook snippet suggestion: if fallback_rate > 5% for 5m OR tail_latency_99 > SLA threshold for 3m, escalate to oncall, enact traffic shedding policy, and roll to previous stable version. Document the exact paging flow.
mike_pm: I'll add that runbook section. Timeline: aim to merge PRD by end of week, engineering scoping and infra estimates next week.
lina_prod: I'll compile the customer impact matrix and prioritize asks (predictability > price, but some customers will accept reduced model quality for cost savings). Deliverable tomorrow EOD.
raj_infra: Preliminary cost delta: +25% infra spend for reserved pools to guarantee tail latency at current model mix. Will add a breakout by machine type in the PRD.
mike_pm: Can we include quantization/variant recommendation matrix in the PRD? Impact on latency, cost, and quality.
anya_eng: Yes — I'll add a small table: FP16 vs int8 vs 4bit quant impacts (latency/cost/regression risk) + recommended auto-fallback thresholds.
sam_sre: Alerting thresholds: set warning at 50% error-budget use, page at 90% over rolling 24h. Also set healthcheck for model liveness every 30s.
mike_pm: Great. Once we have these updates, I'll ask design for the SLA wording and legal for contract language.
deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwoodinc/prds/pull/412 — reviewers requested: @anya_eng, @sam_sre, @lina_prod
anya_eng: Assigning self to technical section and load test plan. Will add a simple k6 script and perf dashboard queries.
sam_sre: I'll draft SLO alerting policies + templates for oncall playbook.
lina_prod: Will prepare customer-facing FAQ and downgrade notice templates.
raj_infra: Adding machine-type cost table and conservative scaling knobs.
mike_pm: Thanks all. If no blockers, plan to merge Friday. :thumbsup:
